config.title: Build notification service API

intro.title: Build notification service API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification service API using Node.js and Express. You will learn to create endpoints that allow a client to send notifications, such as email or SMS alerts, to users. The core programming concept involves handling HTTP requests, structuring RESTful routes, and managing data flow. You'll work with key technologies like Express for routing and middleware, and JSON for data exchange. By the end, you'll have a functional API that can receive and process notification requests.
intro.usecase: Notification service APIs are foundational to modern applications that require real-time user engagement. You'll find them powering notification centers in platforms like Slack, GitHub, and banking apps, where users receive alerts about messages, pull requests, or transactions. As a developer, you'll build these APIs to handle email confirmations, push notifications for mobile apps, and in-app alerts that keep users informed about system events. This pattern is essential for creating responsive applications that maintain user awareness and drive interaction.

objectives: Construct a Node.js server using Express to handle HTTP requests for notifications.
Configure middleware to parse incoming JSON payloads in notification requests.
Implement a POST endpoint to receive and validate notification data.
Initialize and integrate a service module to process and store notification messages.
Manipulate response objects to return appropriate HTTP status codes and messages.
Apply routing structures to organize API endpoints for different notification types.
Control error handling within the API to manage invalid requests gracefully.

steps.title: Add middleware to parse JSON requests
steps.instruction: Add the Express JSON parsing middleware to your app using app.use(express.json()).
steps.hint: Call app.use() with express.json() as the argument to enable JSON body parsing for incoming requests.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding middleware in Express
app.use(express.json());
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be configured to automatically parse JSON request bodies.
successCriteria: The app.use(express.json()) middleware is added to your Express app.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.use() with express.json() as shown in the example.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to add app.use(express.json()) to enable JSON parsing for incoming requests.

steps.title: Create GET /notifications endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a GET route at '/notifications' that returns the notifications array as JSON.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the route path and a callback function that sends the notifications array using res.json().
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET route at '/notifications' is created that will return the notifications array as JSON when accessed.
successCriteria: The route uses app.get() with '/notifications' and sends the notifications array using res.json().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.get() with '/notifications' and returning the notifications array with res.json().
steps.feedbackWrong: The GET endpoint isn't set up correctly. Check that you're using app.get() with the correct route and sending the notifications array as JSON.

steps.title: Create POST /notifications endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a POST route at '/notifications' that adds new notification objects to the array. Use app.post() with the route path and a callback function that handles the request and response.
steps.hint: The callback function should extract the notification data from req.body, add it to your notifications array, and send back the created notification with a 201 status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route at '/notifications' is implemented that successfully adds new notification objects to the array and returns them with a 201 status.
successCriteria: The code includes app.post('/notifications', callback) with a callback that adds req.body to the notifications array and responds with the created notification and status 201.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your callback function properly adds the notification from req.body to the array and sends a response with status 201.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint is missing or incomplete. Remember to use app.post() with the correct route and a callback that handles the request.

steps.title: Add validation for POST request body
steps.instruction: In your POST /notifications endpoint handler, add validation to check that the request body contains both 'title' and 'message' fields before creating a new notification.
steps.hint: You can check if the required fields exist using conditional statements (if statements). If either field is missing, you should respond with a 400 status and an error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST endpoint will now validate incoming requests and return a 400 error with a descriptive message if required fields are missing.
successCriteria: The POST handler includes validation that checks for both 'title' and 'message' in req.body and returns a 400 response when either is missing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check both 'title' AND 'message' fields and return a proper 400 response when they're missing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation isn't working correctly. Check that you're validating both required fields and returning a 400 status with an error message when validation fails.

steps.title: Create GET /notifications/:id endpoint
steps.instruction: Add a GET route at '/notifications/:id' that finds a notification by its ID and returns it as JSON. If no notification is found, return a 404 status with an appropriate message.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the route path containing a parameter ':id'. Inside the handler, find the notification in the notifications array using the id from req.params. Convert the id to a number before comparing.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new GET endpoint is created that can retrieve a single notification by its ID, with proper error handling for non-existent IDs.
successCriteria: The route '/notifications/:id' is defined with app.get(), finds a notification by ID from the notifications array, returns the notification as JSON if found, and returns a 404 status with a message if not found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the route, but make sure to handle both cases: returning the notification when found and a 404 response when not found.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route isn't working as expected. Check that you're using app.get() with '/notifications/:id', finding the notification by ID, and handling both success and error cases.

steps.title: Add error handling for non-existent notifications
steps.instruction: In the GET /notifications/:id endpoint, add a conditional check to return a 404 status with an error message when the requested notification ID is not found in the notifications array.
steps.hint: After finding the notification, check if it exists. If not, use res.status(404).json() to send an appropriate error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The GET /notifications/:id endpoint should now properly handle requests for non-existent notification IDs by returning a 404 status with an error message.
successCriteria: The GET /notifications/:id endpoint includes a conditional check that returns res.status(404).json() when the notification is not found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the error handling isn't complete. Make sure you're checking if the notification exists and returning a 404 status with an error message when it doesn't.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling for non-existent notifications isn't implemented correctly. You need to add a conditional check after finding the notification, and return a 404 response when the notification doesn't exist.

steps.title: Create DELETE /notifications/:id endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a DELETE route at '/notifications/:id' that removes a notification from the notifications array when a matching ID is found.
steps.hint: Use app.delete() with the same route pattern as the GET endpoint. Find the notification index with findIndex() and remove it with splice().
steps.expectedOutcome: A DELETE route is added that removes notifications by ID and returns appropriate HTTP status codes.
successCriteria: The DELETE route uses app.delete() with '/notifications/:id', finds the notification index, removes it from the array, and handles both success (204) and not found (404) cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your DELETE route finds the notification index, removes it with splice(), and returns 204 for success or 404 if not found.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DELETE endpoint isn't implemented correctly. Check that you're using app.delete(), finding the index, and handling both success and error responses.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Add the app.listen() method to start your Express server on port 3000.
steps.hint: Call app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message when the server starts.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your API will be accessible at http://localhost:3000 when you run the server.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've included both the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added app.listen() with the correct syntax to start the server.
